title: Salar de Atacama, Chile
author: NASA/METI/AIST/Japan Space Systems, and U.S./Japan ASTER Science Team
description: Salar de Atacama (Atacama salt flats) in Chile's Atacama Desert receives 2 mm rain per year. Its attraction are the brines 40 m below ground. They are pumped to the surface into large evaporation pans. After the water has vanished, a yellowish greasy solution is left behind that contains lithium.
